## topology

```{r}
# Install and load igraph package
install.packages("igraph")
library(igraph)

# Example data (replace this with your pole data)
# Assuming each row is Pole, Nearest Neighbor
# Test data for poles and their nearest neighbors
data <- data.frame(
  Pole = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C", "D", "D", "E", "E", 
           "F", "F", "G", "G", "H", "H", "I", "I", "J", "J"),
  Neighbor = c("B", "C", "A", "D", "A", "D", "B", "E", "D", "F", 
               "E", "G", "F", "H", "G", "I", "H", "J", "I", "A")
)

# Print out the data
print(data)

# Create graph
g <- graph_from_data_frame(data, directed = FALSE)

# Plot the graph to visualize the topology
plot(g)

# You can also calculate various properties
degrees <- degree(g)
# ... and other analyses as needed

print(degrees)

# Assuming 'g' is your graph object from the previous example

# Calculate the shortest path between two poles, say A and E
path_result = shortest_paths(g, from = "A", to = "E")

# The length of the path (number of links)
path_length = lengths(path_result$vpath)[1] - 1

# Print the path length
print(path_length)

```
